article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 65% Sativa / 35% Indica
Genetics: Wedding Cake × Super Lemon Haze
Breeder: The Cali Connection
THC Content: 18–22%
CBD Content: 1% or less
Terpene Profile: ocimene, limonene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Tart lemon, sweet citrus, earth, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 69–74 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid to late October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Lemon Tart approaches citrus cannabis from two very different directions. Super Lemon Haze brings the unmistakable blast of lemon zest, sharp herbs, and energetic Haze character, while Wedding Cake places a denser layer of sweetness, earth, cream, and resin underneath. The Cali Connection combined the two to create a sativa-dominant hybrid that smells brighter than its dessert-inspired name suggests. Fresh flowers can resemble lemon peel rubbed between the fingers, but breaking the buds apart reveals sweeter pastry, damp earth, herbs, and pepper hiding beneath the citrus.

The effects mirror that layered aroma. A lively cerebral rise generally arrives first, encouraging focus, creativity, conversation, and activity, while a milder physical calm gradually develops later. The breeder places this cannabis strain at approximately 65% sativa and 35% indica and emphasizes its exceptionally resinous colas, making Lemon Tart as interesting to extraction-oriented growers as it is to consumers searching for energetic lemon-flavored weed. With a flowering period of roughly 69–74 days, it asks for more patience than many compact hybrids but rewards that extra time with strong aroma and heavy trichome coverage.
Genetics and Lineage

The official Cali Connection lineage is Wedding Cake crossed with Super Lemon Haze. Wedding Cake contributes much of the dense flower structure, resin, sweet earth, and creamy richness. The cultivar is widely associated with Triangle Kush and Animal Mints ancestry, bringing together OG-influenced fuel and earth with the sweet, minty, dough-like character that became prominent in modern American cannabis. Its presence prevents Lemon Tart from becoming a purely narrow-leaved Haze expression and adds considerable weight to both the buds and the later stages of the high.

Super Lemon Haze provides the brighter half of the pedigree. Originally developed from Lemon Skunk and Super Silver Haze , it became one of the defining citrus-forward sativas of the modern seed era. Lemon Skunk supplies penetrating citrus and Skunk character, while Super Silver Haze adds the deeper combination of incense, spice, herbs, and soaring cerebral energy associated with Haze breeding. The result is a parent known for both unmistakable lemon fragrance and a long-lasting, active experience.

Bringing these families together gives Lemon Tart a particularly useful genetic contrast. Super Lemon Haze stretches the aroma toward tart citrus and lifts the mental effects, while Wedding Cake adds sweetness, resin, flower density, and physical balance. The result is not simply a lemon-flavored Wedding Cake or a sweeter Super Lemon Haze. Good phenotypes express both families simultaneously, combining bright Haze energy with enough Cookies-and-Kush-derived weight to keep the experience from feeling thin or excessively racy.
Effects and Experience

Lemon Tart usually begins with a noticeable cerebral lift. Attention sharpens, mood rises, and tasks that seemed routine can suddenly become more engaging. The experience is often described as focused and energetic rather than scattered, making moderate amounts suitable for creative projects, gaming, music, light outdoor activity, or social situations. The Haze influence is particularly noticeable during this early period, when thoughts may move more quickly and sensory details become easier to notice.

Physical relaxation arrives more gradually. Wedding Cake ancestry adds a warmer body sensation beneath the initial mental energy, preventing the strain from remaining relentlessly stimulating for the entire session. The transition can be especially pleasant during the afternoon: motivation remains intact while muscular tension begins to ease. As the high develops further, the physical component may become more noticeable without necessarily turning into couch-lock.

Potency is generally substantial but not automatically extreme. Commercial examples commonly fall around the upper teens to low 20% THC range, although individual phenotypes and carefully cultivated harvests can exceed that level. Larger servings may make the Haze side feel restless or mentally intense, particularly for people sensitive to THC. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, and temporary anxiety are possible when too much is consumed. Smaller doses usually preserve the cultivar’s best balance of uplift, focus, and later relaxation.
Medical Benefits

Lemon Tart may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer an active daytime profile over pronounced sedation. Its initial cerebral character may help some people feel more engaged when fatigue, low motivation, or stress makes ordinary activities difficult to begin. The uplifting effect can also make repetitive thoughts feel less dominant for certain consumers, although strongly cerebral THC can produce the opposite response in people who are prone to cannabis-related anxiety.

The physical side is gentler but still relevant. As Wedding Cake influence becomes more apparent, muscular tension and general discomfort may feel less intrusive without immediately ending productivity. Some consumers may find this balance useful when dealing with discomfort during daytime hours and do not want the stronger body heaviness associated with traditional indica strains. Appetite stimulation can also develop, while the later phase may feel calm enough for relaxed evening use.

Ocimene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene are commonly associated with Lemon Tart flower. Ocimene can contribute sweet, herbal, and citrus-like aromas, limonene reinforces the sharp lemon character, and caryophyllene adds peppery spice while interacting with CB2 cannabinoid receptors. These compounds help shape the sensory experience, but they should not be treated as individual medical therapies. Anyone using cannabis therapeutically should consider the actual cannabinoid and terpene testing of the flower, personal tolerance, medications, and professional medical guidance.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Lemon Tart earns its name most clearly through aroma. Opening a properly cured container can release an immediate wave of lemon zest, citrus oil, and tart fruit. The impression is sharper than lemon candy and often closer to freshly grated peel, especially in Super Lemon Haze-dominant phenotypes. Sweetness begins to appear underneath after a few moments, softening the citrus with a creamy, almost baked-goods quality.

Breaking apart the flower reveals the darker portion of the profile. Earth, dry herbs, pepper, and faint Haze spice rise behind the fruit, while Wedding Cake contributes a dough-like sweetness that gives the bouquet more depth. Ocimene and limonene help explain the bright top notes, whereas caryophyllene contributes much of the pepper and dry spice. Certain examples may also display light pine or floral qualities depending on phenotype and cultivation conditions.

Flavor develops in a similar sequence. Tart lemon and sweet citrus often dominate the inhale, followed by earthy herbs and mild spice through the middle. The exhale can leave a creamier, lightly nutty or pastry-like sweetness on the palate, creating the contrast suggested by the Lemon Tart name. Vaporization emphasizes the citrus and sweet herbal components particularly well, while combustion tends to make the earthy Haze and pepper more obvious. A slow, cool cure is valuable because the volatile lemon compounds are among the easiest parts of the profile to lose through overdrying.
Growing Information

Lemon Tart grows with the vigor expected from Super Lemon Haze while developing denser, more resinous flowers through the Wedding Cake side. The Cali Connection describes the finished genetics as approximately 65% sativa, and cultivators should plan for noticeable vertical growth during the transition into flowering. Indoor growers with limited height can benefit from topping or early low-stress training, spreading the plant horizontally before the stretch accelerates.

A trellis is particularly useful for creating an even canopy and supporting the resin-heavy colas that develop later. The plant can produce medium-to-tall growth with long flowering sites rather than the squat structure of a traditional indica. Selective removal of weak lower branches helps direct energy toward better-lit flowers, while enough foliage should remain to support vigorous photosynthesis. Strong lighting and adequate root volume allow the cultivar to take advantage of its hybrid vigor.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 69–74 days, or roughly ten to ten and a half weeks. That is longer than many Wedding Cake hybrids but comparatively manageable for cannabis carrying substantial Super Lemon Haze ancestry. Growers should resist harvesting simply because the calendar has reached week nine; much of the final swelling and resin development occurs toward the end of the cycle. Trichome appearance and overall flower maturity provide a better guide than a rigid date.

The breeder highlights resin production rather than publishing a fixed yield number. Mature colas can become heavily coated with trichomes, making Lemon Tart particularly attractive for concentrate production. Some secondary sources describe good production when environmental conditions are strong, but it is more accurate to consider yield moderate to high rather than attach an artificial guaranteed number. Lighting, plant size, training method, container volume, irrigation, and vegetative duration will determine the final harvest.

Late-flowering environmental control deserves attention because resinous colas can become dense. Continuous airflow through the canopy and moderate humidity help prevent moisture from remaining around interior flower tissue. Nutrient strength should remain appropriate for the growing medium rather than being pushed simply because the plant is vigorous. Super Lemon Haze ancestry can encourage rapid growth, but healthy roots and stable irrigation are more useful than aggressive feeding.

Outdoors, Lemon Tart performs best where the season remains favorable into October. A flowering cycle approaching 74 days generally places harvest around mid- to late October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates, depending on latitude and when flowering begins naturally. Full sun, abundant root space, and protection from prolonged autumn rain can produce substantial plants. Growers in cooler or wetter climates may find greenhouse cultivation particularly useful because it provides the extra finishing time needed to mature the resinous colas without exposing them to repeated storms.
FAQ
What strains make Lemon Tart?

The Cali Connection created Lemon Tart by crossing Wedding Cake with Super Lemon Haze. Wedding Cake contributes dense resinous flowers, sweetness, earth, and physical balance, while Super Lemon Haze provides tart citrus aroma, vigorous sativa growth, and energetic cerebral effects.
Is Lemon Tart indica or sativa?

Lemon Tart is a sativa-dominant hybrid. The Cali Connection lists it at approximately 65% sativa and 35% indica. Its effects generally begin energetic, focused, and uplifting before a calmer physical component develops later.
How strong is Lemon Tart?

Commercial examples commonly test around 18–22% THC, although individual plants can be stronger depending on phenotype, environment, maturity, and testing methodology. CBD is usually low. Its stimulating Haze influence can make high doses feel more intense than the THC percentage alone might suggest.
What does Lemon Tart taste like?

Tart lemon and sweet citrus dominate the flavor, followed by earth, herbs, peppery spice, and a creamy pastry-like sweetness. Super Lemon Haze drives the sharp lemon character, while Wedding Cake adds the sweeter and heavier background.
How long does Lemon Tart take to flower?

The Cali Connection lists a flowering period of approximately 69–74 days. That equals roughly ten to ten and a half weeks indoors. Outdoors, plants generally need enough favorable weather to mature around mid- to late October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Final Thoughts on Lemon Tart

Lemon Tart works because its parents solve different parts of the same breeding problem. Super Lemon Haze delivers loud citrus, energy, and unmistakable Haze character, but Wedding Cake adds the density, resin, sweetness, and physical balance that make the finished hybrid feel more substantial. Neither parent disappears inside the cross.

The result is especially appealing to consumers who enjoy citrus cannabis but want more complexity than straightforward lemon flavor. Tart peel and citrus oil sit above earth, herbs, pepper, cream, and sweet pastry, creating a profile that becomes deeper as the flower is broken apart or vaporized. Effects follow the same trajectory, moving from alert cerebral stimulation toward a calmer body sensation as the session progresses.

Growers need to account for the longer 69-to-74-day flowering period and the vertical enthusiasm inherited from Super Lemon Haze, but the cultivar rewards that patience with heavily resinous colas. Training, trellising, airflow, and careful late-flower humidity control are the most useful tools for making the genetics perform well indoors. Outdoor cultivators benefit from a warm autumn or protected greenhouse environment.

For anyone searching for a sativa-dominant lemon strain with more body, sweetness, and extraction potential than a conventional Haze, Lemon Tart occupies a particularly useful niche. It brings the bright personality of Super Lemon Haze into a denser Wedding Cake framework, creating cannabis that tastes energetic before the effects even begin.
